titre: Xbox Confirms Project Helix Is 'a Console Capable of Playing Games From Your PC'... And Is 'Not a PC That Can Also Play Console Games'
Xbox Confirms Project Helix Is 'a Console Capable of Playing Games From Your PC'
chapo: Xbox has confirmed Project Helix is "designed to be a console capable of playing games from your PC."
extrait: Xbox has confirmed Project Helix is "designed to be a console capable of playing games from your PC." Microsoft unveiled a slew of details about its past, present, and future with the surprise publication of the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine. It's all part of surprise festivities meant to help celebrate 25 years of Xbox, and it also happens to have revealed more information about Project Helix than we've received in some time. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has called the next-gen project a "family of devices" before, and although that language is used again here, vice president of next generation Jason Ronald helped paint a clearer picture. The main idea here is that, through the ups and downs of Xbox's history, many lessons have been learned. "When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine – one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed," Ronald said. "My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games." These are already big promises for Project Helix, which has been speculated to arrive as soon as late 2027, but what actually is it? There's no telling when we'll see what the family of devices it encompasses looks like, but today, Ronald was at least willing to sell Xbox fans on the idea of a project that seems to be centered more around the traditional idea of a console than anything else. "We're very clear on the design goal: Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a Pc that can also play console games," he added. "The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customizability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it." Ronald said creating the next-gen project over the years hasn't just meant answering the questions of today, though; it's meant thinking ahead, too. Without directly addressing how it may pertain to the mysterious Xbox project, Ronald pointed to how Generation Alpha adapted to a world where content isn't locked to any one device.
